lesson.fox_portrait.title: Fox Portrait
lesson.fox_portrait.summary: Practice proportion, placement and refined details while building a thoughtful front-facing fox portrait.
lesson.fox_portrait.step.head: Start by establishing the overall head proportion. Compare its height and width before refining the contour.
lesson.fox_portrait.help.head: Look at the widest part of the head and the distance from the crown to the chin. Aim for balance, not perfect symmetry.
lesson.fox_portrait.step.muzzle: Build the cheek planes and muzzle inside the larger head shape. Notice how the muzzle sits below the center.
lesson.fox_portrait.help.muzzle: Compare the left and right spaces around the muzzle. Small differences are natural; focus on the overall relationship.
lesson.fox_portrait.step.ears: Place the ears from the upper head and use a light eye line to judge where the features will sit.
lesson.fox_portrait.help.ears: Check the ear angles against the center of the face, then compare their height before adding detail.
lesson.fox_portrait.step.face: Add the eyes, nose and mouth as landmarks. Work from larger distances first, then refine each shape.
lesson.fox_portrait.help.face: Before changing a feature, compare its distance to the center line, muzzle and nearby eye.
lesson.fox_portrait.step.fur: Finish with a few directional fur accents and brow shapes. Use fewer intentional marks instead of filling every space.
lesson.fox_portrait.help.fur: Let the fur marks follow the direction of the face contour. You can invent your own texture pattern.
lesson.fox_portrait.complete.drawing: Your fox portrait has structure, proportion and your own line character.
